An unretouched photograph taken by a mountaineer kneeling in the snow at about 8,000 metres on K2: camera 40 cm from the subject, 50mm lens at f/4, 1/1000s, ISO 100, looking down at about 35 degrees. It looks like a real frame from expedition documentary footage, with real-world imperfections.

THE MOMENT: in a gap between dark, frost-covered granite rocks, the Spraymax bottle from the reference photos lies on its side, half buried in fresh powder snow, exactly in the orientation shown in image 1: cap pointing to the left, front label facing up toward the camera, the "Spraymax" wordmark reading normally from left to right with upright letters. A climber's gloved hand (a thick black-and-red down mountaineering mitt crusted with frost and snow) has just swept the snow off the front of the bottle and is resting at the right edge of the frame. Loose powder is still sliding off the bottle and a few snow crystals cling to the label.

THE BOTTLE: image 1 and image 2 are real photos of the actual bottle held in a hand indoors; image 3 is its front label artwork. Use them only for the bottle's exact shape, materials and label; ignore the hand, the wall and the indoor light. A slim cylinder about 14 cm long with a rounded shoulder; slightly greyish off-white, semi-matte, opaque plastic; a matte white finely ribbed collar; a white spray pump; a cloudy translucent overcap with the pump visible inside. A white label wraps the body: "Spraymax" in royal indigo-blue rounded letters, large and clearly legible; the small line "Instant Hair Volume & Texture"; and a dark navy ocean-wave photo band toward the base end with "FOR ALL HAIR TYPES" in white. Same letters, colours and proportions as the references; the label follows the curve of the bottle; no other text on it. It is a new bottle: plastic and label clean and intact, with no dirt, stains, scratches, tears or peeling edges.

HOW IT SITS IN THE SNOW: the underside of the bottle is pressed into the snow with a soft blue shadow beneath it; snow is piled against its sides and partly over the base end; a thin dusting of snow and fine ice crystals on the cap and collar; the cold plastic has tiny frost specks. The top edge of the bottle is seen against the dark rock behind it, so the white bottle stands out clearly from the snow.

LIGHT: low afternoon sun from the left, raking across the snow so the crystals sparkle; cold, clear high-altitude light with deep blue shadows; the label side is lit and readable. True daylight colour: no golden or orange tint, no glow, no studio lighting.

CAMERA LOOK: bottle and glove sharp, with focus on the wordmark; the nearest snow and the rocks behind fall off into natural blur; a few wisps of wind-blown spindrift cross the background. The bottle has the same grain, contrast and colour balance as the snow around it. Fine natural grain.

COMPOSITION: vertical 9:16. The bottle lies across the middle of the frame, about 60 percent of the frame width, slightly tilted; the glove enters from the right edge; dark rock fills the upper part of the frame.

No faces, no people other than the gloved hand, no added text, captions, logos or watermarks. Natural and imperfect, not a polished 3D render.
